[pro_tips] Carry an ice axe (and crampons in early season) even though most of the traverse is rock — snow lingers in the connecting basin.

name: Northwest Ridge (Standard Route)
text: [overview] A remote scramble up Wing Peak's northwest ridge from Tailgunner Pass, mixing steep snow faces and rock benches with a final exposed snow/ice finger and short Class 4 summit block;
[beta] Parties approach via the Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Creek drainage to Tailgunner Pass, then climb steep snow faces and rock benches along the peak's northwest ridge.
[beta] The crux is a roughly 70-degree, heavily exposed snowfinger just below the summit, above which loose Class 4 rock leads to the top.
[hazards] Steep, potentially refrozen snow on the Tailgunner Couloir and northwest ridge requiring crampons and an ice axe..
[obj_haz] steep refrozen snow/ice.
[watch_out] The crux snowfinger below the summit is reported at roughly 70 degrees and severely exposed — a slip here would be consequential..
[watch_out] Loose Class 4 rock on the final summit block, especially hazardous when wet or dusted with snow..
[watch_out] A rock defile with deep moats below the summit snow face has been called the most unnerving part of the descent..
[watch_out] north-aspect snow patches are firm enough to walk on..
[gear] snow pickets.
[gear] crampons.
[gear] ice axe.

[detailed_rack] Parties have climbed the route with a single 30m rope, one snow picket, and about six assorted slings for protecting the snowfinger crux and building rappel anchors off the summit and upper snow face.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — standard for the couloir and ridge snow

name: East Face Variation
text: [approach_variants] From the Alpental / Snow Lake trailhead at about 3,100 ft, hike or skin toward Source Lake, then turn south into the basin beneath The Tooth's east face.

[approach_variants] Roughly December to April, and only when the upper mixed ground has built up enough snow and ice to climb and protect — first climbed in winter 1995 and genuinely condition-dependent.
[approach_variants] Steep unconsolidated snow on the final pitch, prone to sloughing.
[approach_variants] And the finish confirms it: the last pitch is steep snow, belayed off small trees, trending slightly right to finish near the summit.

[beta] The crux pitch climbs this corner at about 5.8-ish with one short aid move (A0) or M5 mixed climbing to a tree belay, after which a final pitch of steep snow (using small trees for anchors) trends slightly right to finish near the summit.
[hazards] Steep unconsolidated snow on the final pitch can be avalanche- or slough-prone
[obj_haz] steep unconsolidated snow
[watch_out] Second pitch features long run-outs on thin ice with difficult screw/picket protection;
[watch_out] Corniced terrain on descent;
[gear] crampons.
[what_to_bring] approach skis or snowshoes for the Source Lake basin approach.

[approach] From the Alpental/Snow Lake trailhead (~3,100 ft, 1.5 mi north of I-90 Exit 52 via Alpental Rd), hike/skin up the main trail toward Source Lake, then turn south into the valley/basin below The Tooth's east face.
[turnaround] back off early if ice/snow coverage on the crux corner looks thin or the approach shows avalanche warning signs.
[pitch_detail] Moderate snow/rock (summer East Face line).
